body.statement: Using \(\mathsf{CensusHandle}\), determine \(d_e(G)\) for every rooted graph-query orbit with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\) over characteristic zero. In particular, either certify the supplied five-vertex quartic in \(A_K=S_G^{-1}(R_{\mathrm{inc}}/I_G)\) or exhibit the first strict loss between the prescribed-orientation count and the SEM coordinate degree; any strict loss must be incorporated into the recurrence sought in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\).
body.justification: This is the bounded destructive test that can invalidate the uncorrected orientation-realization conjecture before the all-size proof is attempted.
body.gap: The five-node computations of Foygel, Draisma, and Drton classify whole graphs and selected whole-fiber degrees, not every original-edge coordinate degree under the rooted excess-arrow budget in the \(S_G\)-localized prime incidence algebra.
body.consumer: The frontier proof receives certified base cases or a concrete correction term, and fasttreeid receives a complete small-instance regression suite.

obligation.what_is_open: The exhaustive characteristic-zero census of every rooted graph-query orbit with \(n\le5\) and \(k\le2\).
obligation.obstruction: The supplied computation enumerated orientation graphs but did not enumerate mixed-graph bidirected supports and original-edge queries modulo rooted isomorphism, nor produce saturated rational-univariate certificates for all of them.
obligation.attempted: I lifted the supplied modular quartic to an exact rational Groebner basis and matched its four simple branches to the multihomogeneous coefficient.
obligation.partial_result:
For
\[
D=\{0\to1,0\to2,1\to3,2\to3,1\to4,2\to4\},\qquad
B=\{0\leftrightarrow i:1\le i\le4\},
\]
query \(f=\lambda_{24}\). At the rational source point with directed coefficients \((a,b,c,d,u,f)=(2,3,4,5,6,7)\), disturbance diagonal \((30,31,32,33,34)\), and \(\omega_{0i}=i\), strict diagonal dominance gives \(\Omega\succ0\), and
\[
\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}
30&61&92&707&1014\\
61&155&187&1561&2247\\
92&187&314&2327&3332\\
707&1561&2327&17981&25747\\
1014&2247&3332&25747&36972
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The six residuals are
\[
\begin{aligned}
&30ab-92a-61b+187,\\
&61ac+92ad-707a-155c-187d+1561,\\
&61au+92af-1014a-155u-187f+2247,\\
&61bc+92bd-707b-187c-314d+2327,\\
&61bu+92bf-1014b-187u-314f+3332,\\
&155cu+187cf-2247c+187du+314df-3332d-1561u-2327f+25747.
\end{aligned}
\]
Exact rational Buchberger reduction gives the lexicographic basis
\[
\begin{aligned}
0={}&384915840a+425450175590061f^3-8965411803407607f^2\\
&+62974399432228195f-147445028655847225,\\
0={}&741827520b-593375419233f^3+12321625507347f^2\\
&-85271405126447f+196665729339485,\\
0={}&615040c+25798931271f^3-543666188277f^2\\
&+3818873142057f-8941504654939,\\
0={}&4d-3f+1,\\
0={}&153760u+8599643757f^3-181222062759f^2\\
&+1272957714019f-2980501654153,
\end{aligned}
\]
together with
\[
q(f)=(f-7)(8599643757f^3-181150021425f^2
+1271943861499f-2976933819575).
\]
The exact Euclidean algorithm gives \(\gcd(q,q')=1\). The five linear equations recover one value of every other coefficient from each root, so the specialized ideal consists of four reduced points with distinct \(f\)-coordinates. The block graph is \(K_4\) with exponents \((1,1,2,2)\), and
\[
[X_1X_2X_3^2X_4^2]\prod_{i<j}(X_i+X_j)=4.
\]
The multihomogeneous upper bound and the four simple formal branches imply the characteristic-zero identity \(d_{\,2\to4}(G)=4\). This lifts the modular quartic, but the other rooted orbits with \(n\le5\), \(k\le2\) remain uncensused.
